text: Separating, and working out arrangements for your children? Here's a quick guide from Saltbush and Reed Family Law. Courts decide parenting arrangements based on the best interests of the child, including the safety of the child and the people who care for them. Since May 2024, the law no longer uses the term equal shared parental responsibility, which was often misread as equal time. Before applying to court, you usually need to try family dispute resolution, unless it isn't suitable, for example because of family violence or child abuse. At dispute resolution, you can develop a parenting plan, and agreements can be formalised as consent orders at court. If you're separating, our team can help. Speak with Saltbush and Reed.
